The four panel titles occupy separate bands above their own panels (SVG y=22.52 for the top row, y=349.64 for the bottom row) and the six legend labels sit in two clearly separated rows (SVG y=678.48 and y=697.98) with about 155 pt of horizontal clearance between columns. rubric.legibility: pass, with two encoding defects recorded as findings 1 and 2. Four titled poloidal panels in a 2x2 grid -- 'Limited, 553 cells', 'Limited, 2,105 cells', 'Diverted, 550 cells', 'Diverted, 2,098 cells' (titles decoded from the SVG's subsetted glyph runs and confirmed on the render). Each panel draws nested teal flux contours, the first wall as a solid charcoal closed curve, and a single filled triangle at the magnetic axis; the two diverted panels additionally show a cross marker at the lower X-point. One frameless two-row, three-column figure-level legend sits below the panels. The quantity the caption certifies -- a solved field lying on its analytic reference -- is visible where the two differ, most clearly along the top of the Limited, 2,105 cells panel, where the charcoal dashes separate from the teal by several pixels. The panel-to-panel shape difference is read at a glance. Findings 1 and 2 concern how the two series and the two null sets are encoded, not whether the panels can be read.
rubric.table_form: pass. The figure depicts poloidal flux contours, a wall and null locations -- a spatial relationship that no table carries; the captions' per-row residuals are supplied as text on the page, not as an image of a table.

findings.evidence: attached image-0.png; 4.17x re-render of `git show df88cc593:docs/figures/converged-forward-solve/read-correction-path/terminal-forward-states.svg`; SVG glyph defs m0ef2673822 (retained axis, half-extent 3.25), mb4e7775de4 (reference axis, 4.75), mcbcf22836c (retained saddle, 3.75), m81311702d2 (reference saddle, 5.25) and their <use> coordinates; caption at docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/read-correction-path.html:24
findings.summary: Both null sets are drawn in every panel, but the two marks nest inside one another at sub-pixel separation and cannot be told apart, so the caption's claim that the figure 'draws the wall, both magnetic axes, and both admitted saddles' is not verifiable from the render. The reference marker is drawn from a larger glyph centred on the retained one, and the two centroids coincide: in the Limited, 553 cells panel the retained axis sits at SVG (270.414, 174.890) and the reference axis at (270.416, 174.838), a 0.05 pt separation (0.07 px at the delivered 1400 px render), with glyph half-extents 3.25 pt and 4.75 pt. In a 4.17x render that composite reads unmistakably as a single teal triangle with a thick charcoal border, not as two markers; the legend's 'retained axis' and 'reference axis' swatches, by contrast, are two triangles of different sizes standing apart. The diverted saddles behave the same way: retained (232.585, 615.062) against reference (232.050, 615.011), 0.54 pt apart, with half-extents 3.75 pt and 5.25 pt, so the two crosses fuse into one blocky mark with dark corners showing. The consequence for a reader is that no axis or saddle offset can be seen at all, and a null mismatch between the solved and analytic fields of the size these rows are being certified against would be invisible in this idiom; the caption's numeric residuals are the only place that agreement can be read. Recorded as follow-on and not blocking: every panel remains readable, and the nesting does convey coincidence, which is the intended meaning.

findings.evidence: attached image-0.png; 4.17x re-render; SVG style blocks (`stroke: #1f6f8b; stroke-width: 2` x32, `stroke: #333333; stroke-width: 2.4` x33 with `stroke-dasharray: 8.88,3.84` x33); colour-classified scanlines at y=640, 700 and 760 of the 4200x3000 render; caption at docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/read-correction-path.html:24
findings.summary: The analytic reference is drawn heavier and darker than the solved field it lies beneath, so at the delivered resolution the reference is not a separable second series and the contour edge reads as ragged stipple rather than as two curves. Measured in the source: 33 dashed charcoal (#333333) reference paths at stroke-width 2.4 against 32 solid teal (#1f6f8b) retained paths at stroke-width 2.0. A horizontal scanline through the Limited, 553 cells panel of the 4.17x render shows each contour as a run of teal with charcoal appearing only as a one- to two-pixel sliver on the flanks and only where a dash falls -- so at the 1400 px width the reader receives, the reference is roughly a one-pixel intermittent fringe on the teal line. Where the fields diverge slightly the charcoal protrudes beyond the teal and the composite edge breaks into dark specks; this is most visible in the Limited, 553 cells panel, whose coarse mesh already gives a blocky contour, so a reader cannot separate mesh jaggedness from the double-draw texture. The caption explains the intended reading ('they read as one line with a dashed edge; that agreement is the result'), and that reading does survive where the two series separate -- most clearly along the top of the Limited, 2,105 cells panel, where the dashes stand several pixels clear of the teal. The defect is that the repository's layering rule calls for the beneath series to be thinner and lighter than the subject, and here it is 20 percent thicker and considerably darker, which puts the visual weight of every contour on the baseline rather than on the certified solved field. Recorded as follow-on and not blocking: no series is lost, the separation is still readable where the fields differ, and no label or mark is obscured.

item_verdicts.caption_independence: The caption is not a restatement of a title. The figure carries no title -- identity is in the file name and the caption -- and the caption names each panel with its terminal residual (4.6e-15, 1.3e-14, 9.0e-14, and the strict xfail at 0.0262), states the encoding ('solved contours are drawn on top as thinner solid blue lines over the dashed charcoal analytic reference, on one shared physical level array'), states the read ('Where the fields agree, they read as one line with a dashed edge'), and records the job, the device and the render check. It is independent of the title and it is accurate about the drawing it describes: the solved series really is drawn thinner (2.0 pt) than the reference (2.4 pt) and on top of it. Its claim that the figure 'draws the wall, both magnetic axes, and both admitted saddles' is accurate about what is drawn, and finding 1 records that the result is not visible to a reader.
item_verdicts.finding_materiality: Two follow-on findings, no blocking finding. No label is clipped (0 non-white pixels in the outer 3 px frame), no label overlaps another label or the data, no text is unreadable, and the figure does not depict tabular data, so none of the blocking categories is met.
